summary_en: This Phase II trial tests adding stereotactic ablative radiation therapy (SABR) to standard immunotherapy for people with unresectable or metastatic renal cell carcinoma. The radiation is given in 3 sessions over 1 to 3 weeks, and immunotherapy continues while the disease does not progress and side effects are acceptable. The main outcome is not stated in the record; this is a randomized Phase II study.
summary_es: Este ensayo de fase II evalúa agregar radioterapia estereotáctica ablativa (SABR) a la inmunoterapia estándar para personas con carcinoma de células renales no resecable o metastásico. La radiación se administra en 3 sesiones durante 1 a 3 semanas, y la inmunoterapia continúa mientras la enfermedad no progrese y los efectos secundarios sean aceptables. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; se trata de un estudio aleatorizado de fase II.
who_for: Kidney cancer (renal cell carcinoma) confirmed by tissue testing
Lymph node-positive unresectable or metastatic disease on recent scans
IMDC intermediate or poor risk disease
Measurable disease outside the primary kidney tumor
Not recommended for, or refused, immediate nephrectomy
not_for: Planned definitive treatment of all metastatic sites
Untreated or unstable brain metastases or cranial epidural disease
Systemic therapy for metastatic kidney cancer started more than 90 days before registration
Active autoimmune disease needing ongoing steroids or immunosuppressants
Pregnancy, or unwillingness to stop breastfeeding
